role.altitude: The bioengineer keeps framing studies, watching the process, choosing experiment factors, directing runs and deciding changes; copying batch data, building run tables by hand and writing protocols and reports from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading process data from the historian
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who spends study time on the floor and in the data, not in copying.

tasks.short: Frame the study, pull batch and process data, observe the process and talk with operators, lead study meetings, decide changes in process sequences or operation protocols, and write the study report.

steps.what: Engineer defines the study question and plan
Engineer gathers batch records, process data and deviations for the process
Engineer observes the process on the floor and talks with operators
Engineer leads study meetings with production and quality
Engineer decides which changes in process sequences or operation protocols to recommend
Engineer writes the study report with the recommended changes

loop.input: The data tables, the engineer's recommended changes and the report template.
loop.output: A draft report with data sections filled and a first text for findings.
loop.check: Every number must match a data table; the engineer rewrites findings and recommendations.
loop.stop: The engineer keeps the draft, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each study has its own findings.

tasks.design: Batch records, process data and deviations come from the electronic batch record and process historian as a filtered view per process step and batch, instead of being copied from batch sheets into a spreadsheet. Observing the process, leading the meetings and deciding the changes stay with the engineer. The report template fills the data sections from the same tables, and a drafting step writes a first text the engineer rewrites, with every number matched to a table. Data are viewed per batch, not per operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Batch data sat on paper sheets and in separate files.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic batch records and historian views.
tasks.still_hard: Older lines with paper batch records.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why operators skip a step in the protocol.
tasks.altitude: Less copying; the study itself stays.

reach.learn: Whether changes are based on more batches.

evidence.claim: Time studies checking presence, behaviour or performance need works council consent.
In a writing experiment with 453 professionals, not engineers, a model cut time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.

assumptions: Boundary: leading process studies; reviewing processes for yield opportunities (task 21859) and reports for regulators or publication (task 21856) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: electronic batch records and historian data kept by production, for about 70% of batches; s2 is priced at that share.
Data are used per batch; any timing of individual operators needs works council consent first.
Observing, meetings and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of lines with electronic batch records.
research_questions: Are studies completed sooner and based on more batches?

incremental.description: Engineer checks historian views against batch records for a sample.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: paper batch records; high: electronic records on all lines.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review earlier runs, choose factors and objectives, build the run table, write the protocol, direct bench or pilot production experiments, compile yield and cost per run, and judge which scale-up method optimizes yield and cost.

steps.what: Engineer reviews results of earlier runs for the process
Engineer chooses the factors, levels and objectives for yield and cost
Engineer builds the run table with run order and conditions
Engineer writes the experiment protocol and batch instructions
Engineer directs the bench or pilot production runs with technicians
Engineer compiles product yield and cost per run
Engineer judges which scale of production methods will optimize yield and minimize costs

tasks.design: Earlier run results come from the experiment database as a view per process and condition, instead of searching run files. Choosing factors and objectives stays with the engineer. Design-of-experiments software builds the run table with run order and randomisation from the chosen factors and levels. The protocol template reuses standard sections and fills the run conditions from the table. Directing the runs and judging the scale-up stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Run tables and protocols were built by hand in spreadsheets and documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Design-of-experiments software, experiment databases and protocol templates.
tasks.still_hard: New processes with no earlier runs.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing factors that matter at scale, not only on the bench.
tasks.altitude: Less building tables and protocols; experimenting stays.

evidence.claim: Design-of-experiments software builds randomised run tables from factors and levels.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and directing scale-up experiments; follow-up experiments (task 21846) and recommending specifications (task 21858) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: earlier results kept in the experiment database by sibling task 21853, for about 70% of runs; s1 is priced at that share.
s6 is part of compiling bench and pilot results, which sibling task 21858 covers; its saving is counted there.
Choosing factors, directing runs and judging keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of scale-up studies per year.
research_questions: Do experiments reach a decision in fewer runs?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the protocol template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new processes without earlier runs; high: repeat scale-up studies with templates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
